[augernised] cool thanks. here are 10 other studies summarising benefits, let me know if you want another 10
Strength and power (2025 meta-analysis, 69 RCTs, 1,937 participants) — found creatine plus resistance training significantly improves upper and lower body strength and power. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12430374/
Cognitive function in adults (2024 systematic review, 16 RCTs, 492 participants) — found creatine may benefit memory, attention, and information processing speed. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39070254/
Soccer performance (systematic review to 2019) — examined creatine's effect on aerobic, phosphagen, and anaerobic performance in soccer players. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6520963/
Older adults (2024 meta-analysis, 20 studies, 1,093 participants) — found creatine combined with exercise training significantly improved strength (1RM) in older adults. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12506341/
Endurance performance in trained populations (2023 systematic review) — evaluated creatine monohydrate's effects on endurance outcomes. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36877404/
Metabolic performance (2023 meta-analysis) — found creatine had a more pronounced effect during aerobic and anaerobic exercise versus placebo, including in endurance sports. https://www.cureus.com/articles/184876-effectiveness-of-crea…
Kidney safety (2025 meta-analysis) — concluded creatine is associated only with a modest, transient rise in serum creatinine, not true kidney impairment, with no significant change in GFR. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41199218/
Mental disorders systematic review (2025, five RCTs) — reviewed creatine's effect on depression and bipolar depression symptoms as an adjunct treatment. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12823350/
Depression augmentation trial (Lyoo et al., published in American Journal of Psychiatry, 2012) — a placebo-controlled trial finding creatine augmentation improved depression scores in women with major depressive disorder on an SSRI. https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/25/NCT02922725/Pro…
Depression meta-analysis (British Journal of Nutrition, 2025) — synthesised RCT evidence on creatine as an add-on treatment for depressive symptoms. https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-n…

The clear research is the beta alanine has side effects on few in form of itchiness/tingling that does or doesn’t go away long after ceasing the usage. Beta alanine is added in pre workout supplements.
Now the debated part is that some people get itchiness/tingling after using creatine monohydrate, the counter argument people say that people experiencing it maybe using adulterated creatine (with beta alanine in it) even if the package says 100% pure. Since the majority source of creatine is China the counter agrumentorgs say that QC or deliberate adulteration might be at play here.
